name: analyze_pcap
title: Diagnose SIP calls with an LLM
description:
Diagnose the SIP calls in a capture with an LLM: a written explanation of each call
(why it failed, dropped, rang out, or had one-way or choppy audio) plus the
deterministic quality score and MOS.

Calls an LLM: tens of seconds to minutes, and with a cloud provider (anthropic,
openai, azure) the extracted SIP/SDP data (addresses, users, authentication
headers with their credentials masked) leaves this machine, so ask the user first. For numbers only, quick_quality_check
answers in seconds without an LLM. Needs SIP in the capture; for anything else use
analyze_network_pcap. Without provider it uses the server's SONIC_LLM_PROVIDER, else
ollama; list_llm_providers says which.

Returns a JSON object with status, output.diagnostic_report (per-call findings,
overall assessment, recommendations), quality_analysis (call_quality and
mos_analysis when enabled), sip_data and auth_data; on failure
{"status": "error", "error": "..."}, for example "No SIP data found".
For example, analyze_pcap(file_path="/captures/call.pcapng", provider="ollama", model="fast").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

provider.description:
LLM provider: "ollama" (local), "anthropic", "openai" or "azure".
Default: the server's SONIC_LLM_PROVIDER, else "ollama". Cloud providers need
their API key in the server's environment or in the env file named by
--env-file or SONIC_ENV_FILE.

model.description:
"fast" (small model, quickest), "detailed" (the provider's default model),
"deep" (its most capable model, for example claude-opus-5-5) or "combined"
(fast and detailed, recommended).

enable_quality.description: Also run the deterministic call quality scoring (default true).

enable_mos.description: Also run the RTP MOS analysis per stream (default true).

annotations.title: Diagnose SIP calls with an LLM

name: quick_quality_check
title: Score SIP/RTP call quality without an LLM
description:
Score SIP/RTP call quality without an LLM: the first tool for "how good were the
calls in this capture". Deterministic, a few seconds.

Runs the weighted call quality scoring (network, protocol, codec and completion
scores, an overall score and a grade A+ to F) and the RTP MOS analysis per stream
(ITU-T G.107 E-model: average, worst and best MOS, a category, and what degraded
it). Needs SIP in the capture; for other traffic use analyze_network_pcap. For a
written diagnosis of why a call failed, follow with analyze_pcap (LLM).

Returns a JSON object with status, file, quality_analysis (overall_score, grade,
the four component scores and their details, quality_factors,
degradation_factors) and mos_analysis (streams, average_mos, worst_mos, best_mos,
overall_category, recommendations). A part that failed is reported as
quality_error or mos_error instead. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.
For example, quick_quality_check(file_path="/captures/call.pcapng").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

annotations.title: Score SIP/RTP call quality without an LLM

name: list_llm_providers
title: List LLM providers and configuration
description:
List the LLM providers and models the LLM tools (analyze_pcap,
analyze_pcap_partial_streaming, analyze_batch_pcaps) can use, and whether each
cloud API key is set. No LLM is called; instant. Call it before choosing a
provider other than ollama, or to see which provider an LLM tool uses when a call
does not pass one.

Returns a JSON object with providers (names), models (provider to its "fast",
"detailed" and, for anthropic, "deep" model names), default (used when
SONIC_LLM_PROVIDER is unset), and current_config: provider (what every LLM tool
uses when a call does not pass one) and credentials, which says for each API key only
whether it is configured and where it came from ("environment" or the env file's
path), never any part of the key. For example, list_llm_providers().

name: analyze_batch_pcaps
title: Diagnose every SIP capture in a directory with an LLM
description:
Diagnose every SIP capture in one directory with an LLM, one analyze_pcap run per
file, plus aggregate counts.

Calls an LLM once per file: minutes for a directory. Without provider it uses the
server's SONIC_LLM_PROVIDER, else ollama; a cloud provider receives the SIP data, so
ask the user before choosing one. Reads files matching *.pcap* directly
in the directory (not subdirectories). For one capture use analyze_pcap; for
non-SIP captures call analyze_network_pcap per file.

Returns a JSON object with files (one result per capture) and aggregate
(successful, failed, total_tokens, total_duration); on failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."},
for example when the directory has no pcap files.
For example, analyze_batch_pcaps(directory="/captures/branch-a", provider="ollama").

provider.description:

mode.description: "sequential" (one file at a time, default) or "parallel" (up to 3 at once).

Run the deterministic SIP quality and MOS analysis, then the LLM diagnosis, on one

SONIC_LLM_PROVIDER, else ollama; a cloud provider receives the SIP data, so ask the

LLM provider: "anthropic", "openai" or "azure" stream; "ollama" runs

SONIC_LLM_PROVIDER, else "ollama".

name: analyze_network_pcap
title: Analyze any capture with the network detectors
description:
Analyze any packet capture (not only VoIP) and return deterministic findings as JSON.
The first tool on an unknown capture.

No LLM is used: every verdict comes from decoding the packets (tshark or pure-Go
go-fast L2-L4 decoding), in seconds for a typical capture. It reports which protocols are
present and runs every detector that applies. For a focused answer use
analyze_vpn_pcap (encryption, IPsec, DMVPN) or analyze_routing_pcap (adjacencies,
failover); for SIP call quality, quick_quality_check.

Detectors (pass a subset in `detectors`; the default runs all but the last two):
  - "ipsec": IKEv1/IKEv2 negotiation per IKE SA (outcome: established, failed,
    no_response, auth_likely_failed, ...), the IKEv2 proposals offered and chosen
    (encryption, PRF, integrity, DH group, weak algorithms), KE groups and
    INVALID_KE_PAYLOAD retries, NAT detection hashes checked against the wire and
    the move to UDP 4500, DPD liveness checks, a "diagnosis" per SA (ok,
    proposal_mismatch, dh_group_mismatch, auth_failed, auth_no_reply, nat_t_missing,
    no_reply, liveness_lost, peer_lost_sa), NOTIFY errors, IKE SA collisions, rekeys,
    ESP flows per SPI (sequence gaps, duplicates, an old SPI still used after a newer
    one took over), NAT-T, and the encryption verdict: "encrypted" or
    "cleartext_seen" for traffic between the same two endpoints.
  - "gre_nhrp": GRE tunnels (keys, inner protocols, key mismatch), NHRP registrations
    (spoke -> hub, result registered/refused/unanswered), hub and spoke roles,
    resolution requests/replies, redirects (DMVPN Phase 3), error indications,
    and spoke-to-spoke tunnels.
  - "dmvpn_phase3": per redirected flow the ordered Phase 3 steps (via_hub, redirect,
    resolution_request, resolution_reply, direct) with frames and times, the first
    missing step and why; hub-relayed spoke traffic with no redirect; resolution
    thrashing; and, with `hubs`, encrypted spoke-to-spoke shortcuts (IKE then direct
    ESP) when NHRP is hidden inside ESP.
  - "routing": BGP sessions (state, OPEN AS/hold time/router ID/capabilities,
    keepalive cadence, UPDATE timing, NOTIFICATION code/subcode decoded with a hint,
    the cause of each drop, the MSS of each SYN and SYN-ACK checked against
    `expected_mss`, refused TCP 179), OSPF per link (hello/dead/mask/area/auth/MTU
    mismatches, one-way neighbors, DR/BDR, hello gaps, adjacencies stuck in EXSTART
    or EXCHANGE), EIGRP (K-value and AS mismatches, goodbyes, hold time expiry, INIT
    restarts, queries/SIA), plus a failover_timeline.
  - "reachability": ICMP echo loss/RTT per source->destination pair with outage
    windows, ICMP unreachable/TTL-exceeded with decoded codes, ARP with no reply,
    duplicate IPs.
  - "path_mtu": ICMP Fragmentation Needed / Packet Too Big (router, next-hop MTU,
    the probe frame it refers to), PMTUD black holes (large DF probes or TCP
    segments that vanished with no ICMP while smaller ones got through), IP
    fragments (complete, incomplete, overlapping), reassembly timeouts.
  - "esp_overhead": per ESP SA, packet sizes against cipher families (AES-GCM,
    AES-CBC with SHA1/SHA2, 3DES, NULL), inner size bounds, overhead in tunnel and
    transport-over-GRE mode, tunnel MTU fit, ESP fragmented after encryption.
    Estimates from sizes only; ESP is encrypted.
  - "tcp": per connection: SYN without SYN-ACK, refused, retransmissions (fast or
    timeout), gaps, duplicate ACKs, zero window, window full, RSTs, MSS/window
    scale, RTT and RFC 6298 RTO, and a verdict (no_answer, refused,
    receiver_buffer_exhausted, loss_on_path, receive_window_limited, reset, healthy).
  - "tls": ClientHello SNI, versions, suites, ALPN, groups; ServerHello choice;
    TLS 1.2 certificate (subject, issuer, validity at capture time); cleartext
    alerts; an optional baseline (see options).
  - "qos": DSCP per flow, GRE inner vs outer DSCP, ESP outer DSCP per SA, RTP
    streams with loss, RFC 3550 jitter, DSCP and an E-model MOS estimate, ECN CE.
  - "conversations": protocol mix by packets and bytes, top conversations, top talkers.
  - Run only when named: "cleartext_audit" (audit_cleartext_pcap) and "convergence"
    (analyze_convergence_pcap).

Returns a JSON object: status "success", schema, overall_status ("ok", "warning",
"problem" or "not_present"; the worst detector status, conversations and SIP
excluded), protocols_present, detectors_run, verdicts (detector to one sentence),
issues (severity, stable code, message, Wireshark frame numbers, detector; errors
first), timeline (t in seconds from the first frame, time, protocol, event, detail,
frame), capture (backend, packets, duration, missing tshark fields, warnings), one
section per detector, each with status, verdict and issues, and sip. Lists are cut
at max_items; issues_omitted and timeline_omitted count the rest. On failure
{"status": "error", "error": "..."}, plus valid_detectors for an unknown detector.

Limits: a verdict covers only what crossed the capture point. IKEv2 IKE_AUTH is
encrypted, so the child SA proposal, identities and AUTH are never visible: a PSK
mismatch shows only as a small encrypted IKE_AUTH response or as retransmissions with
no reply (a labelled heuristic). DPD is recognised by message size; INVALID_SPI
normally travels encrypted. ESP with NULL encryption cannot be told apart from real
encryption without keys. With tunnel protection, GRE, NHRP and BGP are inside ESP on
the transport link. OSPFv3 and IS-IS are not decoded.

For example, analyze_network_pcap(file_path="/captures/hub-wan.pcap") or
analyze_network_pcap(file_path="/captures/r1-r2.pcap", detectors=["routing"]).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

detectors.description:
Optional list from ["ipsec", "gre_nhrp", "dmvpn_phase3", "routing",
"reachability", "path_mtu", "esp_overhead", "tcp", "tls", "qos", "conversations"]
(the default), plus "cleartext_audit" and "convergence", which run only when
named. Unknown names return an error listing the valid ones.

peers.description:
Optional list of IP addresses (for example the WAN addresses of the hub
and spokes). The encryption verdict then judges all traffic between any two
of them. Without it, the verdict judges every pair that exchanged IKE/ESP,
plus GRE tunnel endpoints.

display_filter.description:
Optional Wireshark display filter applied before detection,
for example "ip.addr==192.0.2.1" or "not arp". Needs tshark.

max_packets.description: Optional cap on frames read (for very large captures).

include_sip.description:
When SIP is present, also run the existing SIP quality scoring
(no LLM) and attach it under "sip". For full SIP call analysis use analyze_pcap.

max_items.description: Cap on the length of each list in the result (default 25).

since.description: Optional start Unix epoch seconds window bound.

until.description: Optional end Unix epoch seconds window bound.

options.description:
Optional per-detector settings: {"esp_overhead": {"transport_mtu": 1500,
"tunnel_mtu": 1400, "gre_header_bytes": 8}, "tls": {"baseline": {...}}}, the baseline
keys being those of analyze_data_plane_pcap's tls_baseline; also {"dmvpn_phase3":
{"hubs": [hub NBMA IPs]}, "routing": {"expected_mss": 1360}, "cleartext_audit":
{"allow": [tokens]}, "convergence": {"event_time", "failed_peer", "hold_time",
"silence_s"}}. Unknown keys are refused.

annotations.title: Analyze any capture with the network detectors

name: analyze_vpn_pcap
title: Prove VPN encryption and IPsec/DMVPN setup
description:
Prove from packets whether VPN traffic between sites is encrypted and whether the
IPsec and DMVPN overlay formed. Deterministic, no LLM.

Use it on a capture of a WAN/underlay link (between hub and spoke routers). It runs
the "ipsec", "gre_nhrp" and "dmvpn_phase3" detectors of analyze_network_pcap and puts
the answers first:

  - encryption_verdict: "encrypted" (only ESP/IKE/NAT-T keepalives between the
    peers), "cleartext_seen" (some ICMP, GRE without ESP, TCP/UDP payload or routing
    protocol between the same endpoints), "no_esp" (IKE seen but no ESP: the
    tunnel never carried traffic or failed), or "not_present".
  - verdict: one sentence, for example "all inter-site traffic encrypted: 2 peer
    pair(s), 480 ESP packets, no cleartext between the same endpoints" or
    "cleartext seen: icmp 198.51.100.2->192.0.2.1 4 packets".
  - negotiation_verdict: IKE SA outcomes (established, failed with the NOTIFY name,
    no_response, auth_likely_failed).
  - overlay_verdict: NHRP registrations per hub (who registered, who was refused).
  - phase3_verdict: the DMVPN Phase 3 sequence per redirected flow (which step is
    missing when one is), or, with `hubs`, the encrypted spoke-to-spoke shortcuts.
  - ike_diagnoses: one line per IKE SA with a stable code: ok, proposal_mismatch,
    dh_group_mismatch, auth_failed, auth_no_reply, nat_t_missing, udp_4500_blocked,
    no_reply, no_esp_after_auth, liveness_lost, peer_lost_sa. Each SA in
    ipsec.ike_sas also has "negotiation": proposals_offered and proposal_chosen
    (encryption, prf, integrity, dh_group, weak), ke_groups_offered,
    invalid_ke_payload, nat_detection (nat_detected, translated, moved_to_udp_4500)
    and liveness (DPD checks, interval_s_by_sender, unanswered_checks).

Where to capture: on the physical/underlay link, ESP proves encryption. If you
capture on the tunnel interface itself you see decrypted traffic, and GRE without
ESP on the underlay means the tunnel has no IPsec protection. Seconds for a typical
capture.

Returns a JSON object with status, encryption_verdict, verdict, negotiation_verdict,
overlay_verdict, phase3_verdict and ike_diagnoses first, then ipsec (peer_pairs,
cleartext, ike_sas, esp_flows, nat_traversal, issues), gre_nhrp (hubs, spokes,
registrations, resolutions, redirects, error_indications, tunnels,
spoke_to_spoke_tunnels, issues), dmvpn_phase3 (flows, hub_relayed_without_redirect,
resolution_thrashing, encrypted_shortcuts, cannot_show, issues), issues, timeline
and capture. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: IKE_AUTH and everything after it is encrypted. A PSK mismatch is never
visible as a hash: it shows as auth_failed (a small encrypted IKE_AUTH response) or
auth_no_reply (retransmissions, no reply). On a protected DMVPN the NHRP steps are
inside ESP; only the IKE and ESP between spokes can be checked, given `hubs`.

For example, analyze_vpn_pcap(file_path="/captures/hub-wan.pcap",
peers=["192.0.2.1", "198.51.100.2"]).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

peers.description:
Optional list of the VPN endpoints' WAN IP addresses. All traffic between
any two of them is judged. Without it, pairs that spoke IKE/ESP and GRE
endpoints are judged.

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first (needs tshark).

hubs.description:
Optional hub NBMA (WAN) addresses. With them, an IKE SA between two other
addresses is checked as a spoke-to-spoke shortcut (IKE_SA_INIT, IKE_AUTH,
direct ESP).

annotations.title: Prove VPN encryption and IPsec/DMVPN setup

name: analyze_routing_pcap
title: Check routing adjacencies, reachability and failover
description:
Check routing protocol health (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP) and reachability from a capture,
and read a failover in order. Deterministic, no LLM.

Use it to prove that adjacencies formed, to find why they did not (mismatched
timers, AS, K-values, MTU, refused TCP 179, NOTIFICATION codes), or to show how
routing reconverged after a router or link failed. It runs the "routing" and
"reachability" detectors of analyze_network_pcap and puts first:

  - verdict: per protocol, for example "BGP: 1 of 3 session(s) established at
    capture end, 1 session reset(s); problems: BGP_NOTIFICATION."
  - reachability_verdict: ping loss per pair, ICMP errors, ARP without replies.
  - failover_timeline: ordered events with "t" (seconds from the first frame):
    BGP established/notification/down/End-of-RIB/withdraw, OSPF hello_gap,
    neighbor_down/neighbor_up, dr_change, router_silent, EIGRP goodbye,
    hold_expired, adjacency_init, query.
  - ping_outages: runs of consecutive unanswered pings with start, recovery time
    and duration. Compare them with the timeline to measure convergence time.

Capture both sides of an adjacency when you can: a link capture shows hellos from
every router on that link. Issue codes are stable strings, for example
OSPF_HELLO_INTERVAL_MISMATCH, OSPF_MTU_MISMATCH, OSPF_EXSTART_STUCK,
OSPF_EXCHANGE_STUCK, OSPF_ONE_WAY, BGP_TCP_REFUSED, BGP_PEER_SILENT,
BGP_MSS_NOT_CLAMPED, EIGRP_K_VALUE_MISMATCH, EIGRP_NEIGHBOR_SILENT, ICMP_LOSS.
Each BGP session lists "downs" with a cause (hold_timer_expired, notification,
bfd_down, tcp_rst, tcp_fin, hold_timer_expired_inferred) and "tcp_mss" per
connection; each OSPF adjacency has "database_exchange" (stuck: exstart or
exchange, and the cause, for example the DBD MTU mismatch). To time a failover
from an event, analyze_convergence_pcap measures it directly.
Seconds for a typical capture.

Returns a JSON object with status, verdict, reachability_verdict,
failover_timeline and ping_outages first, then routing (bgp sessions, ospf links,
eigrp links, issues), reachability (echo, icmp_errors, arp_unanswered), issues,
timeline and capture. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

For example, analyze_routing_pcap(file_path="/captures/r1-r2-failover.pcap").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

display_filter.description:
Optional Wireshark display filter applied first (needs tshark),
for example "ospf or icmp".

annotations.title: Check routing adjacencies, reachability and failover

name: audit_cleartext_pcap
title: Assert a transport link carried no cleartext
description:
Assert that a crypto transport link carried nothing but allowed traffic: every frame
is checked against an allowlist and the audit passes or fails. Deterministic, no LLM,
seconds for a typical capture.

Use it as a gate after capturing a link: one leaked GRE, BGP, OSPF, ICMP, ARP,
cleartext management session or other frame outside the allowlist fails the audit and
is reported by protocol and address pair with its frame numbers. To explain an IPsec
negotiation instead, use analyze_vpn_pcap.

The default allowlist is ["encrypted"]: IPsec, plus SSH and TLS sessions whose
handshake shows real encryption (the TLS suite in the ServerHello; the SSH cipher from
both KEXINITs). A NULL, anonymous, export or integrity-only TLS suite, or the SSH
cipher none, counts as cleartext and fails; TLS 1.1 and older, RC4/3DES, arcfour and
CBC pass with a WEAK_ENCRYPTION warning; a session whose handshake is not in the
capture passes only as encrypted, unverified (ENCRYPTION_UNVERIFIED), never clean. To
require the IPsec tunnel (the WAN of an IPsec or DMVPN network), pass allow=["crypto"]:
SSH and TLS then fail as ENCRYPTED_OUTSIDE_ALLOWLIST.

Allowlist tokens: encrypted (the default: crypto plus ssh and tls), crypto (IPsec
only: esp, ike, nat-t), esp (IP 50 and ESP-in-UDP), ike (UDP 500/4500), nat-t
(ESP-in-UDP, IKE on 4500, keepalives), ah, arp, icmp, icmpv6, routing (= bgp, ospf,
eigrp, rip, ldp, bfd, pim, vrrp, hsrp) or each by name, gre, l2-control (= cdp, stp,
lldp, lacp, loop: Cisco keepalives, EtherType 0x9000), dhcp, dns, ntp, ssh, netconf,
tls, http2, snmp, syslog, tacacs, radius, tcp:N, udp:N, proto:N, ethertype:0xNNNN.
Scope a token to addresses with @: "icmp@203.0.113.1" (ICMP only to or from the
provider), "bgp@198.51.100.0/30". A Cisco router's transport link also carries
loopback keepalives and CDP: add "l2-control" to accept them.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", passed (true or false), clean (a pass with no
weak or unverified session), result ("pass" or "fail"), verdict, allowlist,
frames_audited, frames_allowed, frames_outside_allowlist, cleartext_frames,
protection, encryption (SSH/TLS sessions by state: encrypted, weak, unverified,
cleartext, not_started), first_violation_frame, by_protocol (protocol, category,
packets, bytes, pairs, first_frame), violations (protocol, category, src, dst,
packets, bytes, first_frame, first_t, last_frame, last_t, frames, hint, reasons),
tcp_sessions (with encryption: state, cipher, version, reason), allowed_by_rule,
issues, cannot_show and capture. Categories: crypto, tunnel_without_encryption (GRE
outside ESP), routing, icmp, layer2, authenticated_only (AH), encrypted,
unencrypted_session (SSH/TLS that negotiated no encryption), cleartext_management,
cleartext. An empty capture fails. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."},
for example for an unknown allowlist token.

Limits (also in cannot_show): only frames that crossed this capture point and that
the capture kept are audited; ESP with NULL or weak encryption passes, because ESP
payload is opaque; a non-first IP fragment follows its datagram's first fragment,
and is reported as udp (fail-closed) when that first fragment was not captured.

For example, audit_cleartext_pcap(file_path="/captures/mgmt.pcap") or, for an IPsec
transport link, audit_cleartext_pcap(file_path="/captures/br1-wan.pcap",
allow=["crypto", "l2-control", "icmp@172.16.11.1"]).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

allow.description: Optional allowlist tokens (see above). An unknown token is an error.

display_filter.description:
Optional Wireshark display filter applied first (needs tshark).
Narrowing the capture also narrows what the audit proves.

max_packets.description: Optional cap on frames read (the audit then covers only those).

max_items.description: Cap on the violations list (default 25; the counts stay complete).

annotations.title: Assert a transport link carried no cleartext

name: analyze_convergence_pcap
title: Time a failover and name what drove it
description:
Measure a failover from one capture and say what drove it. Deterministic, no LLM,
seconds for a typical capture.

From an event (for example the moment a runbook stopped a link or a router) or,
without one, from the first sign of failure, it measures the time to detection, to
the first BGP UPDATE or withdrawal on the surviving path, and to traffic resuming.
Signals: the last ESP/IKE from a peer before it went quiet; IKEv2 DPD checks left
unanswered and the last retransmission (DPD giving up); BGP NOTIFICATIONs (Hold Timer
Expired, Cease/BFD Down), RST or FIN, and a hold expiry inferred from silence; BGP
UPDATEs on sessions not involving the failed peer; ping outages and their recovery;
and on encrypted transport captures the surviving tunnels' ESP rate taking over the
failed tunnel's. For adjacency health without an event, use analyze_routing_pcap.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", verdict, driver (mechanism "bfd",
"bgp_hold_timer", "dpd", "explicit_close" or "undetermined", and reason),
failed_peer and failed_peer_source, event_time, measurements (origin, origin_t,
first_failure_sign, detection, first_update_on_surviving_path, traffic_resumed, and
event_to_first_failure_sign_s, event_to_detection_s, event_to_first_update_s,
event_to_traffic_resumed_s), timeline (t, time, delta_s, phase: event, failure,
teardown, detection, reaction or recovery, signal, peer, detail, frame),
traffic_shift, issues, cannot_show and capture. Deltas are seconds from the event (or
the first failure sign); a negative first-sign delta means the failure showed before
the given event time. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits (also in cannot_show): on a protected tunnel BGP and user traffic are inside
ESP, so the reaction is inferred from ESP rates and the driver from timing against
hold_time; DPD is recognised by size; the event time comes from another clock than
the capture, so a skew shifts every delta; only this capture point is seen.

For example, analyze_convergence_pcap(file_path="/captures/br1-wan.pcap",
event_time="+30") or analyze_convergence_pcap(file_path="/captures/core1-wan.pcap",
event_time="2026-10-27T19:49:30Z", failed_peer="172.16.1.2", hold_time=30).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

event_time.description:
Optional time of the event: epoch seconds, seconds from the first frame
("30" or "+30"), or ISO-8601 with a zone ("2026-10-27T19:49:30Z"). Without it
the earliest failure sign is the start, and a quiet period counts only when the
other side kept sending into it.

failed_peer.description:
Optional address of the peer that failed (a hub's WAN address or a BGP
neighbor). Without it, it is inferred and failed_peer_source says how.

hold_time.description:
Optional BGP hold time in seconds, to infer a hold-timer driven failover
from timing when BGP is inside ESP.

silence_s.description:
Optional seconds of silence that count as a peer stopping. Default:
twice the direction's usual longest gap, at least 3 s, and at least 1.5 DPD
intervals when DPD is periodic.

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first (needs tshark).

max_items.description: Caps the timeline at four times this (default 25).

annotations.title: Time a failover and name what drove it

name: analyze_data_plane_pcap
title: Inspect the data plane: MTU, ESP, TCP, TLS, QoS
description:
Look into the data plane of one capture: path MTU and fragmentation, ESP overhead,
TCP health per connection, TLS handshakes against a baseline, and QoS markings with
RTP quality. Use it after analyze_network_pcap when the question is about packets
getting through (MTU, drops, retransmissions, TLS policy, DSCP, voice quality).

Deterministic, no LLM, one read of the capture: seconds for a typical capture. Needs
only file_path; pass tunnel_mtu (the tunnel's ip mtu, for example 1400) to check that
a full-size packet still fits transport_mtu once encrypted, and tls_baseline (for
example {"versions": ["TLS1.3"]}) to judge TLS against a policy. Runs the path_mtu,
esp_overhead, tcp, tls and qos detectors of analyze_network_pcap.

Returns a JSON object with status, overall_status and one verdict per detector first
(path_mtu_verdict, esp_overhead_verdict, tcp_verdict, tls_verdict, qos_verdict), then
the sections: path_mtu (frag_needed with the advertised MTU and probe frame,
black_holes with the range the path MTU lies in, fragments), esp_overhead (flows with
the cipher families their sizes fit, overhead per mode, outer_fragmentation), tcp
(connections, each with a verdict: no_answer, refused, receiver_buffer_exhausted,
loss_on_path, receive_window_limited, reset, healthy), tls (sessions: SNI, offered and
chosen version and suite, certificate, alerts, baseline_pass) and qos (marked flows,
GRE and ESP marking, rtp_streams with loss, jitter, DSCP and a MOS estimate). Each
section has issues with stable codes (PMTU_BLACK_HOLE, ESP_OUTER_FRAGMENTED,
TCP_ZERO_WINDOW, TLS_BASELINE_VERSION, QOS_RTP_NOT_EF, ...), Wireshark frames, and
limits. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: only what crossed this capture point (a black hole means no ICMP was seen
here); the ESP cipher and mode are estimates from sizes, since ESP is encrypted; the
TLS 1.3 certificate is encrypted; QUIC, DTLS and STARTTLS are not decoded; RTP
latency needs two capture points (correlate_pcaps).

For example, analyze_data_plane_pcap(file_path="/captures/br1-wan.pcap", tunnel_mtu=1400)
or analyze_data_plane_pcap(file_path="/captures/dmz.pcap", tls_baseline={"versions": ["TLS1.3"]}).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

tls_baseline.description:
Optional TLS policy: {"versions": ["TLS1.3"]}, or {"min_version": "TLS1.2",
"cipher_suites": ["TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256", "0x1302"], "require_sni": true,
"alpn": ["h2"], "require_forward_secrecy": true, "forbid_weak_offers": true}.
Without it, versions below TLS 1.2 and weak chosen suites are still flagged.

transport_mtu.description: MTU of the link that carries ESP (default 1500).

tunnel_mtu.description: Optional ip mtu of the tunnel (for example 1400), the largest inner packet.

gre_header_bytes.description:
GRE header inside ESP in transport mode: 8 with a tunnel key
(default, usual for DMVPN), 4 without.

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first (needs tshark).

annotations.title: Inspect the data plane: MTU, ESP, TCP, TLS, QoS

name: correlate_pcaps
title: Follow packets across two or more captures
description:
Follow the same packets through two or more captures taken at different points
(inside and outside of a NAT router, WAN1 and WAN2, before and after a firewall) and
say what happened between them. Use it whenever you have two capture points: it shows
NAT translations, where a reply was dropped, asymmetric paths and probes an ACL stopped,
which one capture cannot.

Deterministic, no LLM. Needs two or more {"path", "label"} entries with unique labels,
taken at the same time (clock_offsets_s corrects clocks that differ). Each capture is
read once and the captures are merged by timestamp as a stream: a packet waits at most
window_s for its copy and at most max_packets_held packets wait at once (the oldest are
evicted early and counted), so memory depends on the window, not the capture size;
seconds for typical lab captures. Packets are recognised by fields NAT leaves alone:
ESP SPI and sequence, TCP sequence/acknowledgement numbers with flags, length and a
payload hash, UDP length and payload hash, ICMP echo sequence with IP identification.
GRE carrying IPv4 is matched on the inner packet.

Returns a JSON object with status, verdict, captures (label, packets, unmatched_packets,
start, end), matching (window_s, max_packets_held, evicted_early, packets_matched), nat
(each translation: at_<label> endpoints, remote, kind, packets, frames), connections
(per conversation, linked through NAT, a verdict: reply_lost such as "the SYN-ACK was
last seen at outside and never reached inside", partial_loss, asymmetric such as "out
through wan1, back through wan2", seen_only_at for a probe stopped after a device while
other traffic between the same addresses crossed it, not_on_other_paths, ok), transit
(time between sightings and TTL decrement per capture pair), dscp_changes, issues and
limits. Frames are given per capture label. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: a device that randomizes TCP sequence numbers or rewrites payloads breaks
matching for those flows; times include clock differences between capturing hosts; a
capture point that was not recording at the time is not counted as missing a packet.

For example, correlate_pcaps(captures=[{"path": "/captures/edge-inside.pcap", "label": "inside"},
{"path": "/captures/edge-outside.pcap", "label": "outside"}]).

captures.description:
Two or more {"path": "/abs/file.pcap", "label": "inside"}; labels unique. List
them in path order when they lie on one path.

window_s.description: Seconds a packet waits for its copy in another capture (default 2.0, at most 60).

max_packets_held.description: Cap on packets held for matching at once (default 200000, at least 100).

clock_offsets_s.description: Optional {label: seconds} added to that capture's timestamps.

max_packets.description: Optional cap on frames read from each capture.

annotations.title: Follow packets across two or more captures

name: merge_pcap_timelines
title: Merge capture timelines and time a failover
description:
Merge the captures of one chaos or failover run into a single event timeline and
measure the time between chosen events against design thresholds. Use it for a
failover run: how long from a link or router going down to routing reconverging and
pings recovering, and whether that is within the threshold.

Deterministic, no LLM. Needs one or more {"path", "label"} entries; each capture is
analyzed once by every analyze_network_pcap detector (seconds per capture), and their
events (BGP down/established, OSPF neighbor_down/up, EIGRP goodbye, ping outages, ICMP
errors, Fragmentation Needed, TCP no_answer/RST/zero window, TLS alerts, ESP
fragmentation, ...) are merged by absolute timestamp, each tagged with its capture
label and detector. A measurement picks two events with selectors, for example
{"name": "wan1 failover", "from": {"capture": "wan1", "event": "down"}, "to": {"event":
"established", "contains": "10.255.0.2"}, "max_s": 30}; selector keys are capture,
detector, protocol, event, contains (substring of the detail) and occurrence ("first",
"last" or a 1-based number), and "to" is searched after "from". Without measurements,
every ping outage and each routing down event paired with the next up event of the same
protocol is measured against failover_max_s. output_path writes the result as JSON so
the run keeps it; it is the only tool that writes a file, and only there.

Returns a JSON object with status, verdict, origin (time of t=0, the earliest capture
start), captures (label, packets, start, end, overall_status, events, verdicts),
measurements (name, from, to, delta_s, max_s, verdict within, exceeded, below_min or
not_found, detail), auto_measurements, timeline (t, time, capture, detector, protocol,
event, detail, frame), timeline_omitted, limits and written_to. On failure
{"status": "error", "error": "..."}, for example for an unknown selector key or an
existing output_path without overwrite.

Limits: events are packet timestamps at each capture point (millisecond precision),
only as comparable as the capturing clocks; timers inside a router between packets are
invisible.

For example, merge_pcap_timelines(captures=[{"path": "/run/wan1.pcap", "label": "wan1"},
{"path": "/run/lan.pcap", "label": "lan"}], failover_max_s=30, output_path="/run/failover.json").

detectors.description: Optional subset of analyze_network_pcap detectors (default all).

failover_max_s.description: Optional threshold in seconds for the automatic measurements.

clock_offsets_s.description: Optional {label: seconds} added to that capture's timestamps.

output_path.description:
Optional absolute path ending in .json to write the result to; refused if
the file exists (unless overwrite) or its directory does not.

annotations.title: Merge capture timelines and time a failover

name: analyze_grpc_pcap
title: Troubleshoot gRPC, gNMI and gNOI from a capture
description:
Troubleshoot gRPC from a capture: gNMI, gNOI, gRIBI, P4Runtime or any gRPC service.
Deterministic, no LLM, a few tshark passes: seconds for a typical capture. Needs
tshark (Wireshark's HTTP/2, HPACK, gRPC, TLS and protobuf dissectors do the decoding).

Finds gRPC wherever it runs: cleartext HTTP/2 by its connection preface on any port,
TLS offering ALPN h2, and the well-known gRPC ports (9339 gNMI/gNOI, 9340 gRIBI, 9559
P4Runtime, 57400 SR Linux and IOS XR, 6030 Arista, 50001 Stratum, 50051, 50052, 32767).
Each flow is named by its service port (the SYN's destination). Per RPC: method, the
grpc-status by name and grpc-message, request and response message counts and sizes,
time to the first response and to the trailers, and a diagnosis. Per connection:
SETTINGS, RST_STREAM and GOAWAY with their error codes (too_many_pings named),
flow-control stalls, PING round trips, frames or header lists over the peer's limits,
TCP resets with RPCs open. gNMI requests and responses are decoded (paths, encoding
against the Capabilities answer, Subscribe mode, notifications, in-band errors) and
gNOI system.Time gives the target's clock. Credentials in gRPC metadata (username,
password, authorization, x-api-key, tokens) are found through HPACK and reported by key
only: values are never returned. TLS without keys shows SNI, ALPN, version, the TLS 1.2
certificate (subject, issuer, validity, DNS and IP SANs) and alerts with what they mean.
TLS is decrypted with a key log (keylog_file) or with the secrets a pcapng carries in a
Decryption Secrets Block (editcap --inject-secrets tls,KEYLOG in.pcap out.pcapng), with
no key log needed; tls_decryption then says, per TLS session, whether it was decrypted
and, when not, why (no secret for its ClientHello random, no ClientHello captured, only
the handshake secrets), with a total.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", schema, overall_status, verdict, summary
(connections, rpcs, rpc_status counts, cleartext_credentials), connections (flow,
service, transport, protocol, services, settings, pings, goaways, rst_streams,
flow_control, credential_keys, metadata_keys, tls), rpcs (flow, stream_id, method,
family, grpc_status, grpc_status_name, grpc_message, request, response, timing,
decoded, diagnosis, frames), credentials (flow, key, cleartext, requests, frames,
value "masked"), tls_decryption (verdict, decrypted, total, secrets_source, sessions:
flow, decrypted, secret_in, labels, reason), issues (stable codes such as
GRPC_UNAUTHENTICATED, GRPC_UNIMPLEMENTED, CLEARTEXT_CREDENTIAL, CREDENTIAL_IN_METADATA,
HTTP2_RST_STREAM, HTTP2_GOAWAY, HTTP2_TOO_MANY_PINGS, HTTP2_FLOW_CONTROL_STALL, TLS_ALERT,
TLS_CERT_NO_IP_SAN, TLS_SESSION_NOT_DECRYPTED, TLS_SECRETS_IN_CAPTURE, with frames),
timeline, capture (tshark version, decode_as, keylog_file_given, tls_secrets,
reread_without_out_of_order, proto_paths) and limits. On failure
{"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits (also in limits): TLS-wrapped gRPC without a key log shows only the handshake
(TLS 1.3 encrypts the certificate too); a capture that starts mid-connection may leave
HPACK headers undecodable; message values are never decoded.

For example, analyze_grpc_pcap(file_path="/captures/gnmi.pcap") or
analyze_grpc_pcap(file_path="/captures/srl.pcapng", keylog_file="/tmp/keys.log").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

keylog_file.description:
Optional TLS key log (SSLKEYLOGFILE format; gnmic writes one with
--log-tls-secret) to decrypt TLS; passed to tshark by path, never copied to the
result (only its labels and ClientHello randoms are read, to say which sessions
it covers). Not needed for a pcapng that carries its own TLS secrets.

proto_paths.description:
Optional directories of .proto files for Wireshark's protobuf dissector
(default SONIC_PROTO_PATH, else ~/.cache/sonic/grpc-protos from
`sonic --fetch-grpc-protos`). Without them gNMI is still decoded.

ports.description: Optional extra TCP ports to decode as HTTP/2.

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first.

max_items.description: Cap on list lengths (connections; RPCs at four times this; default 25).

annotations.title: Troubleshoot gRPC, gNMI and gNOI from a capture

name: analyze_restconf_pcap
title: Troubleshoot RESTCONF and REST from a capture
description:
Troubleshoot RESTCONF (RFC 8040) and REST over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 from a capture.
Deterministic, no LLM, a few tshark passes: seconds for a typical capture. Needs tshark
(Wireshark's HTTP, HTTP/2, HPACK and TLS dissectors do the decoding).

Reads HTTP on the well-known HTTP(S) ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443, ...), on a TLS session
offering ALPN h2 or http/1.1, and on a cleartext HTTP/2 preface on any port. TLS is
decrypted with a key log (keylog_file) or the secrets a pcapng carries in a Decryption
Secrets Block (editcap --inject-secrets tls,KEYLOG in.pcap out.pcapng), with no key log
needed; without one, a TLS session shows only its handshake.

Per request (paired to its response): method, path, HTTP status and phrase, the time
from request to response, request and response Content-Type, response body size, a
Location on a 201 Created, whether it is RESTCONF, and for a RESTCONF error the
ietf-restconf:errors fields (error-type, error-tag, error-app-tag, error-path,
error-message) parsed from the body (JSON or XML). Credentials present are flagged, never
shown: an Authorization scheme (Basic, Bearer) is kept and its credential masked; Cookie,
Set-Cookie and token headers are flagged by name. Over cleartext each is a
CLEARTEXT_CREDENTIAL; over TLS a CREDENTIAL_IN_REQUEST (seen only because the secrets
decrypted it). Message bodies are never decoded except RESTCONF error documents.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", schema, overall_status, verdict, summary
(connections, requests, restconf_requests, status_counts, restconf_errors,
cleartext_credentials), connections (flow, service, transport, http_versions, restconf,
requests, sni, alpn_offered, decrypted), requests (method, path, status, phrase,
request_content_type, response_content_type, request_body_bytes, response_body_bytes,
timing_ms, location, restconf, restconf_errors, credentials, frames), credentials
(flow, header, scheme, kind, cleartext, requests, value "masked"), tls_decryption
(verdict, decrypted, total, secrets_source, sessions), issues (stable codes such as
RESTCONF_ERROR, HTTP_CLIENT_ERROR, HTTP_SERVER_ERROR, HTTP_NO_RESPONSE,
CLEARTEXT_CREDENTIAL, CREDENTIAL_IN_REQUEST, TLS_SESSION_NOT_DECRYPTED,
TLS_SECRETS_IN_CAPTURE, with frames), capture (tshark, decode_as, keylog_file_given,
tls_secrets) and limits. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: TLS-wrapped RESTCONF without a key log shows only the handshake; a capture that
starts mid-connection may leave an HTTP/2 request without its method or path; only
RESTCONF error documents are parsed from a body, never configuration.

For example, analyze_restconf_pcap(file_path="/captures/restconf.pcap") or
analyze_restconf_pcap(file_path="/captures/restconf-tls.pcapng", keylog_file="/tmp/keys.log").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

keylog_file.description:
Optional TLS key log (SSLKEYLOGFILE format) to decrypt TLS; passed to
tshark by path, never copied to the result. Not needed for a pcapng that carries
its own TLS secrets.

ports.description: Optional extra TCP ports to decode as HTTP(S).

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first.

max_items.description: Cap on list lengths (connections; requests at four times this; default 25).

annotations.title: Troubleshoot RESTCONF and REST from a capture

name: analyze_snmp_pcap
title: Name SNMP versions and decrypt SNMPv3
description:
Name every SNMP message's version and decrypt SNMPv3 with a USM users file.
Deterministic, no LLM, one tshark pass: seconds for a typical capture. Needs tshark.

Every message is named v1, v2c or v3, and a v3 message by its security level
(noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv, authPriv); engine discovery is named as such. A v1 or v2c
community string is a cleartext credential (SNMP_CLEARTEXT_COMMUNITY, value masked).
With users_file, each authenticated v3 message says whether it authenticated and each
authPriv message whether it decrypted, and when not, why: unknown_user, unknown_engine
(the user is given for another engine id), auth_failed (wrong auth passphrase),
decrypt_failed (wrong privacy passphrase, or AES-192/256 over an SHA1 or MD5 user, whose
key tshark 3.6.2 extends the Reeder (Cisco) way while net-snmp and other Blumenthal-draft
agents extend it otherwise). An SNMPv3 Report is named by the usmStats counter the agent
returned (usmStatsUnknownUserNames, usmStatsWrongDigests, usmStatsDecryptionErrors, ...).
A decrypted PDU's contents are never returned, only its type and that it decrypted.

The users file is a path on the server (never paste passphrases into the call): block
format, one user per record separated by a blank line, lines user, engine_id (optional),
auth (MD5, SHA, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512), auth_pass, priv (DES, AES, AES-192,
AES-256), priv_pass; or CSV user,auth,auth_pass,priv,priv_pass[,engine_id]. It is handed to
tshark through a private temporary snmp_users table, never on a command line, and no
passphrase is ever returned.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", schema, overall_status, verdict, summary
(messages, versions, v3_security_levels, v3_outcomes, authpriv_decrypted,
authpriv_not_decrypted, cleartext_communities), v3_users (per user: messages, outcomes),
messages (frame, version, security_level, src, dst, pdu, user, engine_id, role, outcome,
reason, report, credential), credentials (protocol, flow, kind, value "masked"), issues
(SNMP_CLEARTEXT_COMMUNITY, SNMP_AUTH_FAILED, SNMP_DECRYPT_FAILED, SNMP_UNKNOWN_USER,
SNMP_UNKNOWN_ENGINE, SNMP_NOT_DECRYPTED, SNMP_AGENT_REPORT, SNMP_USERS_TABLE_REFUSED,
SNMP_USER_NOT_SEEN, with frames), capture and limits. On failure
{"status": "error", "error": "..."}, for example an algorithm tshark 3.6.2 does not offer.

Limits: tshark 3.6.2 offers auth MD5, SHA1, SHA2-224/256/384/512 and priv DES, AES-128,
AES-192, AES-256; a v3 message is decrypted only with the right passphrases.

For example, analyze_snmp_pcap(file_path="/captures/snmp.pcap") or
analyze_snmp_pcap(file_path="/captures/snmpv3.pcap", users_file="/secure/snmp-users.txt").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

users_file.description: Optional path to a USM users file (see above) to decrypt SNMPv3.

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first.

max_items.description: Cap on list lengths (messages at four times this; default 25).

annotations.title: Name SNMP versions and decrypt SNMPv3

name: analyze_aaa_pcap
title: Read TACACS+ and RADIUS with the shared key
description:
Read the TACACS+ and RADIUS exchanges in a capture, de-obfuscated with the shared key.
Deterministic, no LLM, two tshark passes: seconds for a typical capture. Needs tshark.

RADIUS: one row per transaction (Access-Request with Accept, Reject or Challenge;
Accounting Start, Stop, Interim): who asked (User-Name, NAS, Calling-Station), the result,
whether the shared secret validated the Response Authenticator, and the
Message-Authenticator of each side checked as RFC 3579 defines (valid, invalid, absent;
tshark 3.6 does not check it itself). TACACS+: one row per session id with the
authentication result (PASS, FAIL, GETPASS, ...), authorization and accounting status, the
user, action, service and privilege level, and whether the session was sent with the
unencrypted flag (its body in cleartext). With keys_file the TACACS+ bodies are
de-obfuscated and the RADIUS User-Password decrypted; any recovered password is masked
(credential "masked") and never returned, and the shared key is never returned.

The key file is a path on the server (never paste a key into the call): lines
tacacs_key: <key> and/or radius_secret: <key>, or one bare line used for both. It reaches
tshark through a private temporary preferences file, never a command line.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", schema, overall_status, verdict, summary
(radius_transactions, tacacs_sessions, accepts, rejects, cleartext_tacacs_sessions,
credentials_recovered), radius (client, server, id, kind, request_code, response_code,
result, username, nas, calling_station, acct_status, authenticator_valid,
message_authenticator {request, response}, credential, frames), tacacs (session_id,
client, server, user, action, service, priv_lvl, types, authentication, authorization,
accounting, cleartext, credential, frames), credentials (protocol, flow, username, kind,
value "masked"), issues (AAA_ACCESS_REJECT, AAA_NO_RESPONSE, AAA_AUTH_FAIL,
AAA_AUTHORIZATION_FAIL, AAA_CLEARTEXT_TACACS, AAA_CREDENTIAL_RECOVERED,
RADIUS_BAD_AUTHENTICATOR, RADIUS_BAD_MESSAGE_AUTHENTICATOR, RADIUS_NO_MESSAGE_AUTHENTICATOR,
with frames), capture and limits. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: tshark takes one tacplus.key and one radius.shared_secret, so servers with
different keys decrypt only where the key fits; EAP and MS-CHAP are noted, not decrypted.

For example, analyze_aaa_pcap(file_path="/captures/aaa.pcap") or
analyze_aaa_pcap(file_path="/captures/aaa.pcap", keys_file="/secure/aaa-keys.txt").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

keys_file.description: Optional path to the shared-key file (see above).

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first.

annotations.title: Read TACACS+ and RADIUS with the shared key

name: analyze_esp_pcap
title: Decrypt IPsec ESP with SA keys and analyze the inner traffic
description:
Decrypt IPsec ESP with the Security Association keys and run the network detectors over
the inner traffic. Deterministic, no LLM, one tshark pass plus the detectors over the
decrypted packets: seconds for a typical capture. Needs tshark.

For each SA it reports the ESP packets seen and decrypted, tunnel or transport mode, and
tshark's integrity check (icv_good, icv_bad), and when packets did not decrypt, why: a bad
integrity check (wrong integrity key, or for AES-GCM the key and salt), a good integrity
check with no decryption (the integrity key is right, so the encryption key is wrong), or
no packet for that SA at all. A packet counts as decrypted only when its decrypted trailer
is real (RFC 4303 default padding, a real next header, and in tunnel mode an inner IP
packet of exactly the payload's length). The decrypted packets (tunnel mode as sent;
transport mode given back the outer addresses) are rebuilt into a temporary capture and
analysed by the same detectors as analyze_network_pcap; the summary is in inner_analysis.
ESP over UDP 4500 (NAT-T) is decrypted too. Cisco IOS and IOS XE do not expose ESP session
keys, so a Cisco IOS tunnel cannot be decrypted this way: use analyze_vpn_pcap for its
outside view.

The SA file is a path on the server (never paste a key into the call): records separated
by a blank line, lines src, dst, spi, encryption (aes-cbc, aes-gcm, aes-ctr, 3des-cbc,
des-cbc, null), encryption_key (0x hex; for AES-GCM the key followed by its 4-byte salt),
integrity (hmac-sha1-96, hmac-sha256-128, hmac-sha384-192, hmac-sha512-256, hmac-md5-96,
none) and integrity_key; or the output of `ip -s xfrm state`, read as it is. It reaches
tshark as its esp_sa table in a private temporary directory, never a command line, and no
key is ever returned.

Returns a JSON object: status "success", schema, overall_status, verdict, summary
(security_associations, esp_packets, esp_decrypted, sas_decrypting),
security_associations (src, dst, spi, encryption, integrity, packets, decrypted, tunnel,
transport, icv_good, icv_bad, reason), inner_analysis (protocols_present, overall_status,
verdicts per detector, issues), issues (ESP_SA_NOT_DECRYPTED, ESP_SA_PARTIAL,
ESP_SA_NO_PACKETS, ESP_SA_TABLE_REFUSED), capture (sa_count, esp_packets, esp_decrypted,
inner_packets_reconstructed) and limits. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: only ESP matching an SA, with the right key and algorithm, decrypts; a sender
whose padding is not the RFC 4303 default is not recognised as decrypted.

For example, analyze_esp_pcap(file_path="/captures/tunnel.pcap",
sa_file="/secure/xfrm-state.txt").

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

sa_file.description: Path to the SA file or `ip -s xfrm state` output (see above).

detectors.description: Optional subset of network detectors to run over the inner traffic.

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter applied first.

name: diagnose_media_underlay
title: Correlate VoIP quality with underlay and tunnel faults
description:
Run deterministic SIP/RTP quality, MOS, post-200 OK clipping, and RFC 4733 DTMF scoring alongside all network, VPN, routing, and data-plane detectors, and link media impairments directly to co-occurring underlay faults. Deterministic, no LLM, runs both passes concurrently.

Returns a JSON object with status, file, voip (quality_analysis, mos_analysis, media_clipping, dtmf_events), network (full detector verdicts and issues), cross_layer_links (media_symptom, underlay_area, severity, summary, issue_codes, frames), correlated_causes, and verdict. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: correlates faults within the same capture window and relies on packet timestamps and IP/SDP endpoints matching the capture point.

For example, diagnose_media_underlay(file_path="/captures/voip_over_vpn.pcap", peers=["192.0.2.1", "198.51.100.2"]).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

since.description: Optional start Unix epoch seconds window bound.

until.description: Optional end Unix epoch seconds window bound.

annotations.title: Correlate VoIP quality with underlay and tunnel faults

name: diff_pcaps
title: Diff a baseline capture against a broken capture
description:
Compare a known-good baseline capture against a broken target capture concurrently using deterministic network and SIP analyzers without calling an LLM.

Returns a JSON object with status, baseline_file, target_file, overall_status_delta, baseline_packets, target_packets, protocols_added, protocols_removed, issues_added, issues_resolved, tls_deltas (versions, ciphers, alpns, handshakes_delta), tcp_and_mtu_deltas (MSS offered), qos_dscp_deltas, sip_deltas (score, MOS, clipping, DTMF), highlights, and verdict. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: compares deterministic detector outputs at each capture point rather than packet-by-packet wire matching (use correlate_pcaps for hop-by-hop tracking).

For example, diff_pcaps(baseline_path="/captures/good.pcap", target_path="/captures/broken.pcap").

baseline_path.description: Absolute path to the baseline (working) pcap/pcapng capture.

target_path.description: Absolute path to the target (broken) pcap/pcapng capture.

annotations.title: Diff a baseline capture against a broken capture

name: evaluate_capture_gate
title: Evaluate CI network and security policy gates on a capture
description:
Evaluate deterministic CI/CD network and security policy rules over a capture without an LLM. Built-in policies: zero-cleartext, no-weak-crypto, no-critical-issues, mos-min=<float>, and max-clipping-ms=<float>. Defaults to zero-cleartext, no-weak-crypto, and no-critical-issues when policies is omitted.

Returns a JSON object with status, file, passed, exit_code (0 pass, 3 policy violation), policies_applied, results (name, passed, summary, violations with code, detector, severity, message, frames), violation_count, and verdict. On failure {"status": "error", "error": "..."}.

Limits: judges only traffic observed at the capture point; encrypted tunnels require the WAN link capture to verify.

For example, evaluate_capture_gate(file_path="/captures/smoke.pcap", policies=["zero-cleartext", "no-weak-crypto", "mos-min=3.8"]).

file_path.description: Absolute path to a pcap/pcapng file on the machine running this server.

allow.description: Optional allowlist tokens passed to zero-cleartext.

annotations.title: Evaluate CI network and security policy gates on a capture
